description: Adversary Village explores adversary emulation, red teaming tradecraft, active directory tiering attacks, stealthy C2 frameworks, EDR evasion, and offensive automation.

talks.title: New Generation of PEAS
talks.teaser: Carlos Polop presents the new generation of PEAS (LinPEAS/WinPEAS), revealing advanced local privilege escalation techniques across Windows, Linux, and AD.
talks.summary:
The Evolution of Local Privilege Escalation

Local privilege escalation (LPE) has evolved far beyond checking kernel version exploits, searching for unquoted service paths, or scanning SUID binaries.

Automating Multi-Vector Escalation with PEAS

Carlos Polop details the architecture and heuristics behind LinPEAS and WinPEAS, designed to enumerate obscure misconfigurations, cached credentials, and token privileges.

Uncovering Domain Compromise Pathways from Local Access

Polop demonstrates how local system enumeration uncovers Active Directory certificate templates, DPAPI secrets, and service credentials that facilitate full domain compromise.

Hardening Operating Systems Against Automated Auditing

The author provides defensive configuration baselines to eliminate common privilege escalation vectors and audit anomalous process scanning.

talks.title: Designing a C2 Framework
talks.teaser: Daniel Duggan (Rasta Mouse) shares architectural lessons and design patterns for engineering resilient, stealthy Command & Control (C2) frameworks.
talks.summary:
The Renaissance of Open-Source C2 Frameworks

Recent years have seen an explosion in open-source Command & Control (C2) platforms, but building a robust, production-grade framework remains a formidable software engineering challenge.

Architectural Design Patterns for C2 Frameworks

Daniel Duggan explores modular C2 architecture, covering agent-server communication protocols, serialization formats, listener profiles, and asynchronous task queues.

Engineering Resilient and Extensible Implants

Duggan discusses payload design tradecraft, including memory injection primitives, sleep obfuscation, dynamic API resolution, and cross-platform agent execution.

Operational Lessons and Framework Lifecycle Management

The presentation provides red teams with practical guidance on maintaining C2 infrastructure, managing operational telemetry, and avoiding detection signatures.

talks.title: Prelude Operator: Accessible Adversary Emulation
talks.teaser: CALDERA creator David Hunt introduces Prelude Operator, an accessible desktop adversary emulation platform designed to automate offensive security testing.
talks.summary:
Democratizing Adversary Emulation for All Organizations

While advanced adversary emulation is vital for validating defensive controls, complex orchestration frameworks have historically been out of reach for small security teams.

Introducing Prelude Operator

David Hunt presents Prelude Operator, an open-source desktop platform engineered by the original authors of MITRE CALDERA for automated security testing.

Deploying Autonomous Agents and Adversary TTP Chains

Operator deploys lightweight agent implants capable of autonomously executing multi-stage attack chains mapped directly to the MITRE ATT&CK framework.

Measuring Defensive Posture and Continuous Validation

Hunt demonstrates how organizations can use Operator to continuously test EDR detection coverage, validate SIEM alerts, and benchmark security maturity.

talks.title: Scaling Up Offensive Pipelines
talks.teaser: Gil Biton demonstrates building automated CI/CD weaponization pipelines to scale red team payload generation, obfuscation, and EDR evasion testing.
talks.summary:
The Escalating Complexity of Modern Endpoint Protection

Next-generation EDR solutions with behavioral analysis and cloud telemetry force red teams to invest extensive time engineering evasive payload weaponization pipelines.

Building Automated Offensive CI/CD Pipelines

Gil Biton details designing automated weaponization pipelines that compile, obfuscate, and cryptographically sign implants on demand.

Automated EDR Testing and Validation Harnesses

The author showcases automated staging environments where newly compiled payloads are dynamically tested against multiple live EDR agents before operational deployment.

Scaling Red Team and Purple Team Operations

Biton illustrates how automated pipelines streamline adversary emulation workflows, allowing operators to focus on strategic execution rather than manual tooling builds.

talks.title: Tool Demo: ImproHound - Identify AD Tiering Violations
talks.teaser: Jonas Knudsen introduces ImproHound, an open-source tool built on BloodHound data to automatically detect Active Directory tiering violations and dangerous access paths.
talks.summary:
The Challenge of Enforcing Active Directory Tiering

Microsoft's Enterprise Access Model divides Active Directory into three distinct security tiers (Tier 0, Tier 1, Tier 2) to prevent workstation compromise from escalating to domain controllers.

Identifying Lateral Movement Paths in Complex AD Graphs

Jonas Knudsen explains why manual auditing fails in large enterprise directories containing thousands of overlapping ACL permissions and service accounts.

Introducing ImproHound for Automated Tiering Analysis

Knudsen demonstrates ImproHound, an open-source analytical tool that ingests BloodHound graph data to automatically identify tiering violations and high-risk privilege paths.

Remediating Critical Exposure Paths

The author provides administrators with prioritized remediation steps to decouple tiering violations and eliminate dangerous credential exposure.

talks.title: C2Centipede: APT-Level C2 Communications for Common Red Teams
talks.teaser: Jose Garduno introduces C2Centipede, an advanced C2 communication framework implementing Fast Flux, Domain Generation Algorithms (DGA), and resilient relays.
talks.summary:
The Network Resilience Gap in Threat Emulation

While nation-state threat actors employ sophisticated network resilience techniques, most open-source red team C2 tools rely on static domains and single-point HTTP egress.

Architecture of C2Centipede

Jose Garduno introduces C2Centipede, a modular communication framework implementing advanced network tradecraft—including Fast Flux networks, DGAs, and multi-protocol channels.

Resilient Multi-Hop Proxy Relays and Evasion

By dynamically rotating egress nodes and routing beacon traffic through decentralized relays, C2Centipede maintains persistent C2 connectivity across hostile blue team defenses.

Hunting Advanced C2 Channels

Garduno provides defenders with statistical traffic analysis metrics and behavioral heuristics to detect decentralized, algorithmically generated C2 traffic.

talks.title: Exploiting Blue Team OPSEC Failures with RedELK
talks.teaser: Marc Smeets demonstrates using RedELK to track blue team investigations during red team operations, exploiting defensive OPSEC failures to maintain access.
talks.summary:
The Operational Complexity of Modern Red Team Infrastructure

As offensive operations scale across diverse cloud redirectors and multi-stage payloads, managing operational telemetry and monitoring blue team activity becomes vital.

Monitoring Red Team Infrastructure with RedELK

Marc Smeets presents RedELK (Red Team's Elastic Stack), a centralized logging and analytics platform engineered to track all offensive traffic and agent interactions.

Exploiting Blue Team Investigation Footprints

When blue team analysts investigate suspicious endpoints, their automated sandboxes, IP queries, and VirusTotal submissions leave distinct digital footprints across red team infrastructure.

Real-Time Situational Awareness and Counter-Threat Hunting

Smeets shows how red teams use RedELK alerts to identify when defensive teams discover specific infrastructure, enabling timely evasive pivots.

talks.title: Advanced Persistent Threat: A Short History and an Example Attack
talks.teaser: Industry veteran Mark Loveless dissects the origin of the term 'APT', detailing nation-state attribution methodologies using an actual attack on his home network.
talks.summary:
Demystifying the Advanced Persistent Threat (APT)

The term 'APT' is frequently overused in cybersecurity marketing, obscuring the true operational characteristics that distinguish nation-state actors from opportunists.

The Origins and Doctrine of State-Sponsored Cyber Espionage

Mark Loveless traces the historical coining of the term APT in military circles, defining the hallmarks of strategic intent, unlimited resources, and persistent patience.

Case Study: An In-Depth Dissection of a Targeted Intrusion

Using an actual targeted attack attempted against his personal home infrastructure, Loveless analyzes the packet telemetry, reconnaissance cadence, and zero-day tooling used.

Attribution Methodologies and Defensive Mindset

The author outlines rigorous attribution frameworks and advises security teams on building long-term defensive resilience against patient adversaries.

talks.title: PurpleSharp: Automated Adversary Simulation
talks.teaser: Mauricio Velazco presents PurpleSharp, an open-source C# adversary simulation tool that generates realistic Active Directory attack telemetry across Windows environments.
talks.summary:
The Telemetry Deficit in Enterprise Detection Engineering

Blue teams often struggle to build robust detection rules because enterprise environments lack authentic, labeled adversary telemetry to validate alert pipelines.

Introducing PurpleSharp for Active Directory Simulation

Mauricio Velazco releases PurpleSharp, an automated C# tool designed to simulate adversary behavior across Windows and Active Directory domains.

Executing Controlled ATT&CK Technique Playbooks

PurpleSharp executes comprehensive playbooks mapped to MITRE ATT&CK—including Kerberoasting, password spraying, process injection, and WMI lateral movement.

Benchmarking SIEM and EDR Detection Capabilities

Velazco illustrates how purple teams use PurpleSharp to measure telemetry collection rates, validate EDR alerts, and systematically tune detection rules.

talks.title: Everything Is a C2 If You're Brave: Unconventional Egress Channels
talks.teaser: Mauro Eldritch and Luis Ramirez automate unconventional C2 channels, routing command-and-control traffic through messaging apps, social media, and video game servers.
talks.summary:
The Limitations of Traditional Web C2 Channels

Enterprise security perimeter appliances strictly inspect standard HTTP/HTTPS and DNS traffic, flagging abnormal beaconing intervals and newly registered domains.

Weaponizing Legitimate Platforms for Stealthy Egress

Mauro Eldritch and Luis Ramirez demonstrate repurposing trusted third-party cloud platforms as covert Command & Control (C2) message brokers.

Automating Wacky and Unexpected C2 Transports

The authors build working proofs-of-concept routing C2 beacons through messaging apps (Telegram, Discord), social media profiles, and multiplayer video game chat protocols.

Detection Strategies for Unconventional Traffic

The presentation provides blue teams with behavioral heuristics and network anomaly detection methods to spot data exfiltration over legitimate SaaS and gaming platforms.

talks.title: Tenacity: An Adversary Emulation Tool for Persistence
talks.teaser: Atul and Harshal present Tenacity, an adversary emulation tool automating the deployment and testing of complex Windows persistence mechanisms.
talks.summary:
The Critical Importance of Persistence in Adversary Campaigns

Adversaries prioritize persistence mechanisms to maintain long-term access across reboots, accounting for over 30% of top techniques observed in the MITRE ATT&CK framework.

Architecture of the Tenacity Framework

Atul and Harshal introduce Tenacity, an automated adversary emulation toolkit engineered specifically to deploy, manage, and clean up Windows persistence techniques.

Simulating Diverse Persistence Primitives

Tenacity automates scheduled tasks, registry run keys, COM hijacking, service creation, and WMI event subscriptions across enterprise endpoints.

Validating Blue Team Hunting Playbooks

The authors demonstrate how defensive teams can use Tenacity to benchmark baseline persistence detection scripts and validate forensic readiness.

talks.title: Adversary Village Kick-Off
talks.teaser: Abhijith B.R. kicks off the inaugural DEF CON 29 Adversary Village, introducing talks, emulation CTFs, and offensive research tracks.
talks.summary:
This DEF CON talk covers adversary village kick-off.

talks.title: The Way of the Adversary
talks.teaser: Phillip Wylie explores the adversary mindset, offensive philosophy, and psychological motivations essential for effective red teaming and threat emulation.
talks.summary:
Understanding the Mindset of the Adversary

Effective red teaming and offensive assessments require more than mastering technical exploit tools; operators must adopt the mindset and strategic patience of real adversaries.

Deconstructing Adversary Motivations

Phillip Wylie examines the diverse motivations driving cyber threat actors—from financial gain and hacktivism to state-sponsored economic espionage.

Emulating Adversaries Realistically

Wylie explores how adopting authentic adversary philosophy improves threat emulation fidelity, helping blue teams prepare for realistic attack cadences.

Cultivating the Offensive Security Mindset

The presentation offers practical guidance for aspiring offensive security professionals on critical thinking, continuous learning, and ethical tradecraft.

talks.title: Phish Like an APT
talks.teaser: Sanne Maasakkers analyzes real-world nation-state phishing strategies, comparing APT psychological pretexts with traditional red team social engineering.
talks.summary:
Analyzing Real-World APT Phishing Campaigns

While security research heavily documents nation-state malware and exploit chains, the specific social engineering pretexts used to deliver those payloads receive less empirical focus.

Deconstructing Nation-State Phishing Strategies

Sanne Maasakkers investigates real-world APT spear-phishing campaigns, analyzing how threat actors tailor pretexts to target industries, geopolitics, and current events.

Comparing APT Pretexts to Red Team Scenarios

Maasakkers compares sophisticated APT lures with standard commercial red team phishing templates, highlighting common oversights in enterprise simulations.

Building Realistic Threat Emulation Phishing Programs

The author provides red teams with frameworks for designing realistic, high-fidelity phishing campaigns based on genuine threat actor OSINT research.

talks.title: Red Team Credentials Recon: OLD with a TWIST
talks.teaser: Shantanu Khandelwal presents GitHub Credentials Stroller, an automated OSINT reconnaissance tool that deep-scans developer repositories for exposed credentials.
talks.summary:
The Threat of Leaked Developer Credentials on GitHub

Developers frequently commit API keys, cloud credentials, and database passwords to public and corporate GitHub repositories, providing attackers with instant initial access.

Limitations of Existing Credential Scanners

Shantanu Khandelwal reviews existing open-source secret scanning tools, identifying common blind spots in deep commit history analysis and fork enumeration.

Introducing GitHub Credentials Stroller

Khandelwal introduces GitHub Credentials Stroller, a reconnaissance tool that recursively dives into developer organizations, commit diffs, and issue attachments.

Operationalizing Credential Recon for Red Teams

The author demonstrates practical workflows for red teams to harvest initial access credentials and advises organizations on automating secret leakage remediation.

talks.title: Signed, Sealed, Delivered: Comparing Chinese APTs
talks.teaser: Cheryl Biswas analyzes decades of Chinese state-sponsored supply chain intrusions and economic espionage campaigns across global technology sectors.
talks.summary:
A Long History of Software Supply Chain Intrusions

While software supply chain attacks have dominated recent headlines, state-sponsored cyber espionage groups have weaponized trusted vendor channels for over two decades.

Profiling Prominent Chinese APT Groups

Cheryl Biswas profiles leading Chinese threat groups (such as APT10, APT41, and Barium), analyzing their strategic focus on telecommunications, aviation, and software vendors.

Modus Operandi: Stolen Certificates and Trojanized Builds

Biswas examines key tradecraft patterns, including stealing code signing certificates, poisoning upstream software updates, and leveraging digital infrastructure for economic espionage.

Strategic Defense Against Multi-Stage Supply Chain Threats

The author provides enterprise defenders with threat modeling frameworks to assess vendor dependencies and audit third-party trust relationships.

talks.title: How I Got COVID in a Red Team SE and Physical Intrusion
talks.teaser: Daniel Isler recounts an authorized multi-vector physical intrusion and social engineering red team engagement conducted during the COVID-19 pandemic.
talks.summary:
The Value of Full-Scope Multi-Vector Red Teaming

True adversary emulation cannot rely solely on network exploitation; comprehensive assessments must incorporate physical security breaches and human social engineering.

Planning a Multi-Vector Physical and Social Engineering Engagement

Daniel Isler details planning an authorized red team simulation against high-security corporate facilities amidst strict pandemic restrictions.

Executing Physical Infiltration and Social Engineering

Isler recounts tailgating past security checkpoints, cloning access badges, manipulating building staff, and planting rogue hardware implants on internal LANs.

Lessons Learned and Pandemic Operational Challenges

The author shares the unexpected personal hurdle of contracting COVID-19 during the assessment, emphasizing the importance of adaptability and safety protocols in physical security testing.

talks.title: Tradecraft Development in Adversary Simulations
talks.teaser: Fatih Ozavci shares systematic methodologies for developing custom tradecraft, repurposing public tools, and tuning evasion for high-maturity adversary simulations.
talks.summary:
Building Campaign-Specific Adversary Tradecraft

Real-world threat actors rarely develop entirely new tools for every engagement; they strategically select, modify, and repurpose existing open-source and commercial tooling.

Analyzing Tool Selection and Weaponization Tradeoffs

Fatih Ozavci examines the operational calculus behind tool selection, analyzing when to build custom implants versus when to pack and modify public frameworks.

Developing Resilient Evasion Primitives

Ozavci demonstrates practical techniques for modifying public tools to strip known IOCs, implement custom memory loaders, and bypass endpoint inspection hooks.

Structuring Continuous Tradecraft Development

The author provides red team leads with a structured operational pipeline to research, build, and maintain evasive tradecraft across simulation lifecycles.

talks.title: Autonomous Lateral Movement in Linux Environments
talks.teaser: Stephan Wampouille demonstrates autonomous lateral movement in Linux networks, chaining benign system behaviors to traverse internal infrastructure undetected.
talks.summary:
The Concept of Autonomous Lateral Movement

While manual lateral movement requires continuous operator intervention, autonomous implants can parse local telemetry and self-propagate across network segments.

Chaining Benign Behaviors to Evade Detection

Stephan Wampouille illustrates how multiple individually benign Linux commands—such as SSH key discovery, network probing, and cron job inspection—can be chained together.

Automated Telemetry Parsing in RAT Architectures

The author demonstrates an agent architecture that parses remote command responses in real time, automatically extracting new IP targets and injecting credentials into downstream commands.

Defending Linux Networks Against Autonomous Spreading

Wampouille outlines defensive containment strategies, including strict host-based firewalling, ephemeral SSH certificates, and zero-trust network segmentation.

talks.title: From On-Prem to the Cloud: Hybrid AD Attack Path
talks.teaser: Sergey Chubarov demonstrates live attack scenarios bridging on-premises Active Directory and Azure AD, exploiting synchronization flaws to compromise hybrid clouds.
talks.summary:
The Security Realities of Hybrid Active Directory

Most modern enterprises operate hybrid identity architectures, relying on synchronization engines to bridge on-premises Active Directory with Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD).

Mapping Hybrid Lateral Movement Pathways

Sergey Chubarov demonstrates live attack scenarios illustrating how compromising an on-premises workstation or server allows pivoting into cloud identities.

Exploiting Azure AD Connect and Seamless SSO

Chubarov dissects synchronization vulnerabilities, password hash sync extraction, and OAuth consent grant abuse to escalate privileges to Global Administrator.

Hardening Hybrid Identity Deployments

The author provides identity administrators with actionable hardening configurations to isolate tier-0 synchronization servers and implement cloud conditional access.

talks.title: Introduction to Adversary Emulation
talks.teaser: Samuel Kimmons provides a foundational guide to adversary emulation, explaining how threat intelligence and the MITRE ATT&CK framework guide testing.
talks.summary:
The Fundamentals of Threat-Informed Defense

Adversary emulation bridges the gap between vulnerability scanning and real-world defense by systematically replicating the tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) of specific threat actors.

Leveraging Cyber Threat Intelligence (CTI)

Samuel Kimmons explains how to extract actionable TTPs from intelligence reports and map adversary campaigns onto the MITRE ATT&CK matrix.

Structuring Controlled Emulation Engagements

Kimmons walks through engagement lifecycles, from defining testing scope and rules of engagement to coordinating purple team collaboration between red and blue teams.

Measuring and Improving Security Posture

The presentation illustrates how security teams can use emulation results to close defensive gaps, tune SIEM correlation rules, and validate detection engineering.

talks.title: Game Theory: Understanding Strategy and Deception in Adversarial Conflict
talks.teaser: Juneau Jones applies mathematical game theory to cyber conflict, modeling rational adversary decision-making, strategic deception, and payoff matrices.
talks.summary:
Applying Game Theory to Cybersecurity Conflict

Game theory provides mathematical frameworks for studying strategic decision-making between competitive, rational actors in high-stakes environments.

Modeling the Attacker-Defender Payoff Matrix

Juneau Jones models cyber operations as asymmetric, non-zero-sum games, quantifying the cost of attack versus the cost of defense across various scenarios.

Strategic Deception and Information Asymmetry

Jones examines how introducing honeypots, deceptive telemetry, and artificial delays alters adversary payoff calculations, increasing their operational costs and inducing mistakes.

Optimizing Defensive Resource Allocation

The author demonstrates using game-theoretic models to determine optimal investments in preventative controls versus detection and deception capabilities.

talks.title: Operation Bypass: Catch My Payload If You Can
talks.teaser: Matthew Eidelberg breaks down the mechanics of modern EDR evasion, demonstrating API unhooking, AMSI bypasses, and indirect system calls in offensive payloads.
talks.summary:
The Mechanics of Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR)

Modern EDR agents monitor process execution by injecting user-mode DLLs, hooking Win32 APIs, and subscribing to Event Tracing for Windows (ETW) and AMSI telemetry.

Bypassing User-Mode API Hooks and AMSI

Matthew Eidelberg walks through advanced payload evasion techniques, including patching Antimalware Scan Interface (AMSI) buffers and unhooking loaded ntdll.dll modules.

Implementing Direct and Indirect System Calls

By invoking direct and indirect system calls (Syswhispers/Hell's Gate), offensive payloads bypass userland API hooks entirely, communicating directly with the Windows kernel.

Defensive Engineering and Kernel-Level Visibility

Eidelberg advises defensive teams on relying on kernel-level telemetry (ETW Threat Intelligence, kernel callbacks) rather than fragile user-mode hooks.
